result.summary:
Read handoffs/WF02-REQ-035/step-03-test-designer-rework1.json and this run's own prior step-04-test-runner.json FAIL to confirm exactly what changed: TEST-DESIGNER fixed all 8 failing countAuditRows()-based assertions in registrationApproval.db.test.ts (AC10, 3 cases) and organizerRequests.db.test.ts (AC2/AC4/AC6/AC7, 5 cases), which were off by exactly +1 because registration.ts's registerForEvent unconditionally writes a 'registration.request' audit_log row on every outcome including 'requested' -- a pre-existing REQ-034 behavior, untouched by REQ-035. The fix changed hardcoded absolute counts to delta assertions off a captured 'before' baseline, and switched rows[0] reads to rows.find(...) since a registrationId can now legitimately carry more than one audit row. The unused commandUpdate helper (MINOR issue from the original FAIL) was confirmed absent from both the actual test file (grep: no match) and the spec's fenced source (only referenced in the rework note describing its removal, not as live code).

Ran npm run lint -w apps/bot: PASS, clean (`eslint .`, zero errors/warnings). Ran npm run build -w apps/bot: PASS, clean (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`, zero errors).

Ran the full suite twice from repo root with the mandated flag (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism`, never from apps/bot): Run 1 -- 39/39 test files passed, 358/358 tests passed, 41.78s. Run 2 -- 39/39 test files passed, 358/358 tests passed, 43.73s. Both runs identical, zero variance.

Re-ran the concurrency file (apps/bot/src/domain/registrationApproval.db.test.ts) in isolation THREE additional times per this run's instruction (it already passed 5/5 times before this rework; re-confirming since the surrounding file's AC10 baselines changed even though AC5's describe block itself was not touched): all three isolated runs identical -- 7/7 tests passed each time (2.87s, 2.51s, 4.30s). Zero flakiness across all 5 executions of this file in this verification pass (2 embedded in the full-suite runs + 3 standalone).

All 8 previously-failing assertions now pass. All previously-passing ACs (AC1, AC3, AC5, AC8, AC9) remain passing. No spec/behavior mismatch remains.

Total verification: 5/5 clean, deterministic runs (2 full-suite @ 358/358 + 3 isolated concurrency-file @ 7/7), lint clean, build clean.
